verdict.rationale: Glama documents building a developer's own server from a GitHub repo, Dockerfile, npm or PyPI package, and switching it from private to a public listing. Registry server pages ship pre-filled install configs for major clients, ownership can be claimed and verified, and community developers confirm they upload and revise their MCPs on Glama. Missing for 10: documentation of the publish/release flow (a community report says an undocumented credit requirement blocked rebuild and release), and evidence that newly listed servers get effective discovery (a developer reports getting lost among existing servers).

support.subject: As a developer, I can publish my own MCP server on the platform for distribution, discovery, and installation by others

citations.quote: Connect a GitHub repository and Glama builds the image straight from source.
Private by default – flip to public listing when ready.
Every server on the Glama registry ships with a pre-filled config block for both clients – copy it, paste it, done.
Stable, account-bound ownership token copied from the Glama claim panel. Keep it published to retain verified ownership.
I've personally revised my MCPs to improve the quality of the score
